_readme: Copy this file to config.json and fill in your own values. config.json is gitignored.
This holds everything MACHINE-READ or PRIVATE: phone numbers, handles, Chrome
profiles, caps and ramp dates. The bin/ scripts read it directly.
It deliberately does NOT hold brand voice or reply templates. Those live as prose in
brands/<slug>/ because they cannot survive being turned into config fields — a reply
assembled from JSON reads like a form letter, which is the exact failure this project
exists to prevent. Run bin/brand-init.sh <slug> to scaffold a brand kit from here.

schedule._note: Used by bin/due.sh to decide what to run in a loop. DM first on purpose: answering someone who already contacted you beats going looking for someone who hasn't.

budget_floor._note: Leads stating a budget below this are rejected — see social-prospect. Set null to disable.

_field_notes.wa_number: Digits only, country code, no + or spaces. bin/wa-link.sh reads this.
_field_notes.enabled: false blocks ALL activity for that account, prospecting included.
_field_notes.ramp_start: YYYY-MM-DD, the date public replies were cleared. null = 0 replies/day, forever. This is how a read-only trial stays read-only: the agent physically cannot reply until a human sets a date.
_field_notes.daily_cap: Steady-state ceiling after the ramp completes.
_field_notes.chrome_profile: Which Chrome profile this brand is logged in to. One profile per brand is what stops brands replying as each other. NOTE: nothing enforces this — the extension attaches to whichever Chrome is connected. It is a label for you, and a reminder to confirm the logged-in account on screen before acting. A per-platform accounts.<platform>.profile still overrides it if you genuinely split a brand across profiles.
_field_notes.excluded_areas: Places people repeatedly ask about that you do NOT serve. Lets the agent decline consistently instead of re-deciding.
